title: The Lighter Brief
overview: Washington had a busy Tuesday: the House shelved an impeachment push against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, House Republicans picked Jim Jordan as their next leader, and the Supreme Court heard a case that could change how agencies fine businesses. Closer to home, Charlotte is cleaning up a diesel spill. On the brighter side, Jamaica has a newly merged high school, a schoolboy football cup is back, and Da Brat is bringing a hip-hop Nutcracker to Chicago.

stories.headline: House sets aside Hegseth impeachment effort, for now
stories.summary: The House voted 211-204 to send articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth back to committee, which effectively ends the effort for this session of Congress. The push was led by Republican Rep. Thomas Massie, who accused Hegseth of high crimes related to military operations, including strikes on Iran and on alleged drug boats. Hegseth and President Trump both defended his record. Democrats, who take control of Congress in January, have promised investigations.
key_facts: Vote was 211-204 to refer the articles to committee
This was Massie's second attempt; the first expired after an early recess before the midterms
Hegseth called Massie a "disgruntled and defeated congressman"
Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, expected to be the next Speaker, said of Hegseth: "He's got to go"
stories.why: The issue may come back once Democrats hold the House majority in January, so it's worth keeping an eye on.

stories.headline: Supreme Court weighs who gets to hand out federal fines
stories.summary: The justices heard arguments over whether the Labor Department can fine a New Jersey farm, Sun Valley Orchards, through its own internal process instead of a jury trial. The department fined the farm about half a million dollars over alleged poor conditions for visa workers, which the farm disputes. The justices seemed divided. The government warned that a ruling against it could disrupt enforcement in programs like Medicare and federal student loans.
key_facts: The case involves the H-2A farmworker visa program
The farm was fined about $500,000; it disputes the charges
Government lawyer Sarah Harris called requiring courts for all civil penalties "the nuclear option"
A decision is expected by the end of June 2027
stories.why: The ruling could change how many federal agencies enforce rules on businesses.

stories.headline: Atrium Health on the hook for Briar Creek diesel cleanup
stories.summary: Diesel fuel from a storage tank at Atrium Health's Mercy Hospital in Charlotte leaked over the weekend, and some of it reached Briar Creek. Mecklenburg County says Atrium must pay for the cleanup and will receive a notice of violation. Any fines will be decided once the full scope of the spill is known.
key_facts: About 2,000 gallons leaked from the tank, according to Storm Water Services
At least 800 gallons are estimated to have reached the creek
The EPA is monitoring the cleanup
Residents are asked to keep themselves and their pets away from the creek until the color and smell are gone
stories.why: If you or your dog walk near Briar Creek, skip the water for now.

stories.headline: Jim Jordan picked to lead House Republicans
stories.summary: House Republicans chose Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan as their minority leader for the next Congress, a week after Democrats won the House majority. Jordan beat current Majority Leader Steve Scalise 106-73 in a secret ballot. A co-founder of the House Freedom Caucus, Jordan pitched himself as experienced in congressional oversight. His win has also renewed attention on decades-old allegations from his time as an Ohio State wrestling coach, which he has consistently denied.
key_facts: Jordan won 106-73 over Steve Scalise
This was his third bid to lead House Republicans, after tries in 2018 and 2023
He takes over on January 3, 2027
He has represented Ohio in the House since 2007
disputed: Reports differ on the size of Republican seat losses: one outlet says more than 40 seats, another says about 30 with 14 races still uncalled
stories.why: Jordan will be the leading Republican voice in the House as Democrats take charge.

stories.headline: Two Jamaican high schools join forces as Hydel Cumberland High
stories.summary: Jamaica's Education Minister Dana Morris Dixon officially launched Hydel Cumberland High School in St Catherine, formed by merging Hydel High and Cumberland High. The Cumberland campus could hold 1,200 students but had just over 300, while Hydel's campus faced infrastructure problems. The new school is adding a traditional sixth form, expanded science classes and plans for an agricultural lab.
key_facts: $70 million has been invested in upgrading the electrical system
The Cumberland campus in Portmore has room for 1,200 students
Principal Carlon Pitt announced the campus's first traditional sixth-form program
The school is positioned as a TVET (technical and vocational) centre of excellence
stories.why: Students get more course options and better facilities by sharing resources.

stories.headline: Jamaica's ISSA Champions Cup is back
stories.summary: The schoolboy football knockout that pits top urban and rural teams against each other returns after a one-year break; there was no 2025 tournament because of Hurricane Melissa. Eight teams, including Kingston College, Jamaica College and Glenmuir High, will compete for the title. The final is set for the National Stadium.
key_facts: Wolmer's Boys vs Kingston Technical playoff: November 12
Quarter-finals: November 20-21
Semi-finals: November 28; final: December 5 at the National Stadium
KC, JC and Glenmuir have each won the cup twice
stories.why: It's a fun sign of normal life returning after the hurricane, with some big matchups possible.

stories.headline: Jamaica says no public money went to the canceled Cardi B concert
stories.summary: Jamaica's Ministry of Culture says the government made no commitment or payment toward a proposed concert featuring Cardi B, calling it a private commercial event. The statement comes amid a dispute between Cardi B and the organizers of BZR WKND after she withdrew from the October show. The ministry says it is limiting event spending while it focuses on hurricane recovery.
key_facts: The festival was scheduled for October 16-18
PM Andrew Holness has directed that funds be redirected to hurricane recovery where possible
disputed: Confirmed: the government says it paid no fees
Reported: Cardi B has threatened legal action against the BZR WKND organizers; the details of the dispute aren't laid out in this coverage
stories.why: It clears up questions about whether public money was involved.

stories.headline: FDA adds rare eye-risk warning to Ozempic, Zepbound and similar drugs
stories.summary: The FDA is requiring 12 GLP-1 drugs to add a warning about NAION, a rare eye condition that can cause sudden vision loss, usually in one eye. The agency's review found the risk is higher for people on these drugs, but still very low overall. Lilly said the communication isn't specific to its medicines and that it will respond promptly.
key_facts: Drugs affected include Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound and Foundayo
In a pooled look at 126 trials, NAION occurred at 6.4 per 100,000 patient-years on GLP-1s vs 3.8 on placebo or other treatments
The review was prompted partly by a 2025 JAMA Ophthalmology study
The FDA announced the change on November 9
disputed: These drugs are already FDA approved; this is a label update, not a recall
Animal data showed no clear mechanism, and NAION risk factors such as diabetes and sleep apnea overlap with conditions common in GLP-1 patients, which makes cause and effect hard to pin down
If you take one of these drugs, talk to your doctor before making changes, and get prompt care for any sudden vision changes
stories.why: It's useful to know if you or someone close to you uses these popular medicines.
